chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, from Sadīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

About a man who has intercourse with a beast, he said: “He is to be flogged less than the hadd punishment, and he must pay the value of the beast to its owner because he has ruined it for him. It is to be slaughtered and burned if it is from those whose meat is eaten. If it is from those ridden on their backs, he must pay its value, and he is to be flogged less than the hadd punishment, and it is to be taken out from the town in which he did that with it to another land where it is not known, then sold there, so that he is not shamed by it.”

key_terms.أَفْسَدَهَا: he rendered it damaged or unusable for its owner
key_terms.دُونَ الْحَدِّ: with a punishment less than the fixed hadd penalty
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الْبَهِيمَةِ: the market value of the beast
key_terms.لَا يُعَيَّرَ بِهَا: so that he is not reproached or shamed because of it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhib al-Ahkam on a man who commits an act with a beast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a man who commits an act with a beast, specifying a discretionary flogging below the hadd level and financial liability for the animal’s value. It also details how the animal is to be dealt with depending on whether it is eaten or ridden, reflecting both punishment and the protection of the owner’s rights.
